consequence.statement: No operational consequence: operators only gain a new opt-in option — writing validation rules with assertion trees; the evidence describes no failure, rejection, ignored setting, or change to existing policies or workloads.

original.statement: Kyverno 1.13 adds the ability to use assertion trees (previously CLI-only, from Kyverno-JSON) as a sub-type of validation rules, so Kyverno policies can also validate non-Kubernetes workloads; the evidence names no schema field for this capability and describes no impact on existing behavior.

decision.reason: [ev-129b0ee1bcce] describes only a new capability: "assertion trees can also be used in validation rules as a sub-type" in Release 1.13. It says nothing about existing policies or workloads failing, being rejected, being ignored or needing migration. The rendered CRD diffs cover apiCall.default and Service appProtocol, which are separate changes and say nothing about this feature's consequence. So the consequence for an operator who does nothing is "none" (informational).
